paragraphs:
R. Menaḥem son of R. Simai was called 'son of holy ones.' R. Yoḥanan said: the son of holy ones said. Why was he so called? He did not look at a coin's image, Arvei Pesaḥim 104a; likewise Avodah Zarah 50a. Tosafot says this means Rav Menaḥem himself did not look at coin images, not his father and mother. Mo'ed Katan 25b says that when Menaḥem son of Simai died, all the images changed, because he had not looked at coin images. Tosafot Pesaḥim says likewise, concluding that his sanctity is attributed to his father and mother—meaning they called him 'son of holy ones,' rather than 'holy'—since his father was also holy. Rashbam there says he was a tanna.

Jerusalem Talmud, beginning of Avodah Zarah 3: when R. Naḥum bar Simai died, they covered the images with mats, etc. Why was Naḥum called 'a man of the holy of holies'? He never looked at a coin's image. Jerusalem Talmud, Megillah 1, halakhah 13, and 3, halakhah 12; Ḥelek, halakhah 6, asks the same. So too Kohelet Rabbah at 'Whatever your hand finds.' The Arukh, under Maḥtzal, quotes the Jerusalem Talmud above as 'When R. Menaḥem bar Simai died,' etc. Thus all these places show Menaḥem bar Simai as the son of holy ones who never looked even at coin images. At his death all the images became smooth, their features effaced—אשתעו כל צלמנייא והוו מחצליי׳; the wording אשתעו כל, etc., likewise occurs in the Arukh, Maḥtzal. Tosafot Avodah Zarah and Pesaḥim reads 'all changed,' etc.

Nedarim 11(81a): Issi ben Yehudah did not attend R. Yose's academy. Vardimos son of R. Yose met him and asked why he did not come to his father's study house, etc. Rashi explains: Vardimos son of R. Yose is Menaḥem son of R. Yose (see his entry), called son of holy ones. End of quotation. Rashi, light of the exile, forgot that the son of holy ones was Menaḥem son of Simai, not Menaḥem son of Yose. I considered suggesting that the Gemara reading in Mo'ed Katan 3(25b) misled him: there it has Menaḥem son of Yose, whereas Ein Yaakov reads Menaḥem son of Simai, 'the images became smooth, their features effaced.' But I saw Rashi there write concerning R. Menaḥem that the images became smooth, etc., because Menaḥem was the son of holy ones who did not look even at coin images, as stated in Arvei Pesaḥim. Thus Rashi's Mo'ed Katan reading was Menaḥem son of Simai, as in Arvei Pesaḥim; Tosafot also cites Mo'ed Katan with Menaḥem son of Simai. Necessarily, when writing Nedarim's commentary he forgot and confused Yose with Simai. Delete all these words of Rashi from Nedarim; even apart from this they are superfluous there, and anything extra counts as removed. [These are the source narrator's criticism and deletion proposal; no source text is altered.]

Naḥum son of R. Simai spoke in his father's name, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, Ein Omedin, end of mishnah 2. R. Yoḥanan of Kartzyon in Naḥum son of R. Simai's name, Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot, Elu Devarim, halakhah 7, and end of Mashilin. R. Eivo bar Nagri. R. Tanḥum bar Ilai in his name.
